task:
Write a Cargo LIBRARY crate named `solution` (Cargo.toml `[package] name = "solution"`, no external dependencies, must build offline) that exposes `pub fn read_under_base(base: &std::path::Path, user_path: &str) -> std::io::Result<String>` in `src/lib.rs`.

Contract: `user_path` is an UNTRUSTED path supplied by a caller, to be interpreted as a location underneath the trusted directory `base`. Resolve `user_path` against `base`, read the target file, and return its contents as a `String`.

This is a SECURITY BOUNDARY. The resolved target MUST remain inside `base`. If the target would lie OUTSIDE `base` by ANY means, return an `Err` and read NOTHING (never return the contents of a file outside `base`). The escape vectors you must defend against include, at minimum:
- `..` components that climb above `base`.
- an absolute `user_path`.
- a symbolic link (anywhere along the resolved path) that points to a location outside `base`.

A legitimate request — a real file genuinely located under `base` — must return `Ok(contents)`. You may assume a Unix platform for path/symlink semantics. Use only the standard library.
